status_reason: The silica cable cannot carry MIR ATR light, and the link length and conditions needed to choose a fiber and approve a field link are missing.
answer: The concept cannot be approved as stated, because the silica cable transmits only about 350-2400 nm while the water-in-oil ATR spectra lie at 4000-2000 cm-1 and need mid-IR fiber. The first step is a laboratory test of MIR ATR on a CIR mid-IR fiber, and a field approval needs the link length and process conditions.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR for water in petroleum on a CIR mid-IR fiber in the laboratory before any link to the other building
inline.probe: ZrO2 ATR probe with the tip sealed in a PEEK shaft and protected by PEEK tubing
inline.install: Laboratory first; the field install point is unknown until the line location and conditions are supplied
inline.fiber: CIR chalcogenide As-S mid-IR fiber (1.1-6.5 um)
inline.test_against: The same ATR probe on a PIR fiber (3-17 um), comparing the 4000-2000 cm-1 spectra
inline.not_final_because: The link length, routing, operating conditions and water range are not supplied; mid-IR reach over distance is not documented; no detection limit is given.

problems.text: The existing silica cable is a visible/NIR fiber that transmits about 350-2400 nm, so it cannot carry MIR ATR light; the water spectra in the slides span 4000-2000 cm-1.
Reach to a building away is not documented for mid-IR fibers: the 100-300 m cables are for low-OH silica (Vis-NIR), and the PIR versus hollow-waveguide comparison covers only 2 m.
Approval is asked before the facts allow it: fiber type, link length, routing and conditions are not supplied, and the method choice depends on them.
The water evidence is a chart for 0.1-2.0 % water with no detection limit, link length or process conditions, so it does not show performance at the client's process range.

methods.why: ATR probes analyse liquids at a distance from the spectrometer using high-transmission mid-IR fibers, and a water-in-petroleum ATR example exists in the slides.
NIR is the most common online fiber method and works with silica cables, but the sources give no NIR water-in-petroleum evidence, so it is a comparison only.
Raman is complementary to MIR but needs special probes, its signals are weak, and fluorescence can mask them.
Fluorimetry relies on secondary emission from certain substances, and most chemicals do not fluoresce; the sources show no fluorescent marker for water.

questions.q: What is the link length and routing from the analyzer to the petroleum line?
questions.why: Mid-IR reach over distance is not documented, and this decides the fiber option.

questions.q: What are the operating conditions of the line (temperature, pressure, flow and sample point)?
questions.why: The chart gives no process conditions, and the probe choice depends on them.

questions.q: What water content range and accuracy must be measured?
questions.why: The evidence covers only 0.1-2.0 % water and gives no detection limit.

questions.q: Do you have independent laboratory water values for the oil samples?
questions.why: Quantitative use needs calibration and validated models, and the reference must come from an independent analysis.

experiment.objective: Confirm that the MIR ATR water signal is visible across the client's water range before any field link is designed.
steps: Prepare oil samples with known water content spanning the client's range, starting from the 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 % levels in the slide.
Record ATR spectra over 4000-2000 cm-1 with the ZrO2 ATR probe on a CIR fiber.
Repeat on a PIR fiber and compare the spectra to see which fiber covers the measured range.
Determine the reference water content of each sample by independent laboratory analysis, not by the instrument's own calibration.
Build a chemometric model on one set of samples and validate it on separate samples.
references: S02 p.13 (ATR probe and water-in-petroleum spectra)
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria to be supplied by the client.

pathway.key_features: Absorbance rises with water content across 4000-2000 cm-1 in the slide chart.
pathway.path_reason: The key features and the process range are not yet known, so the laboratory test comes first (AFS guided pathway step 1).

multispectral.why: Raman is complementary to MIR, but the sources give no oil-water Raman case and Raman signals are weak and easily masked by fluorescence.
multispectral.test: Only if MIR ATR alone fails on the same validation samples; a combination must beat MIR ATR alone on that data.

assumptions: The existing silica cable is Vis-NIR as stated in the enquiry.
The water range is the 0.1-2.0 % range of the slide unless the client states otherwise.
The sample point at the petroleum line is accessible to an ATR probe; this is not yet confirmed.
